title: Reciprocation: The Old Give and Take
coreMove: Pause after a gift or concession and decide whether you received generosity or an obligation device.
sourcePressure: The source covers reciprocation, uninvited debt, free samples, institutional favors, unequal exchange, reciprocal concessions, rejection-then-retreat, and the defense of distinguishing real generosity from imitated generosity.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Do not make this simple gratitude advice; the chapter is about debt pressure that can be deliberately manufactured.

hook: The free gift is never free
You owe more than you think
tryThisNow: Think of one favor you owe
Say thank you without saying yes
examples: coworker buys coffee then asks for help

exampleSpecs.audience: an engaged couple comparing three reception halls
exampleSpecs.stakes: booking an overpriced venue because the tasting felt like hospitality
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coordinator boxes extra pastries before the price discussion, and the couple writes the favor on the quote sheet before deciding
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two sugared tartlets wrapped in gold paper

exampleSpecs.audience: a store owner asked to order a large stack from a distributor
exampleSpecs.stakes: tying up cash in unsold inventory after a distributor sponsors refreshments
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the owner notices the sponsored wine came before the order form and asks whether the quantity would still make sense without it
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a corkscrew lying beside a carton of advance copies
mustAvoid: friendship or liking as main lever

exampleSpecs.domain: municipal vendor breakfast before a procurement vote
exampleSpecs.audience: a new council aide tracking ethics risk
exampleSpecs.stakes: mistaking catered friendliness for neutral information
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the aide maps who ate the vendor's breakfast before the committee softens its questions
exampleSpecs.firstImage: foil trays of egg sandwiches under heat lamps

exampleSpecs.audience: a hobbyist deciding whether to buy an annual kiln package
exampleSpecs.stakes: upgrading after the instructor gifts an extra firing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the hobbyist hears herself justifying the annual package as repayment for the free firing and separates the two
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a wet clay bowl on a wooden bat

exampleSpecs.audience: a hardware store owner approached by a board member
exampleSpecs.stakes: agreeing to a large ad after first refusing an unrealistic title sponsorship
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after declining the title sponsorship, the owner recognizes the smaller program ad as a retreat designed to feel like compromise
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a poster mockup taped to a paint counter

exampleSpecs.domain: software onboarding call for a veterinary clinic
exampleSpecs.audience: a clinic manager evaluating a records platform

skillTargets: detect uninvited debt in an offer sequence
separate sincere favor from compliance setup
choose repayment that does not surrender the larger decision

tryThisNowSpec: Before accepting a free add-on today, say what return action it might be quietly asking from you and whether that return is deserved.
